newsitem.title: USA: Defense rests in Florida doctor's murder trial.
newsitem.headline: Defense rests in Florida doctor's murder trial.

text.p: The defence abruptly rested its case Wednesday in the murder trial of Dr. Ernesto Pinzon, a Colombia-born physician charged with methodically killing a patient as the man's grieving and confused family stood by his hospital bed.

Defence lawyers had said for a month they would close their case with the 37-year-old Pinzon's own testimony explaining he was only trying to relieve a terminal cancer patient's pain when he injected him with massive doses of morphine followed by potassium chloride, a drug often used in lethal injection executions.

But defence lawyer Bill Fletcher said the lawyers changed their minds after a surprise defence witness damaged the credibilty of the state's star witness, the Highlands County medical examiner Dr. Stephen Nelson.
The defence witness, former Broward County, Fla. Chief Medical Examiner Dr. Ronald Wright, testified he had once fired Nelson.
"I fired him for a number of reasons," Wright said. "But the primary reason was dishonesty."

Among the incidents Wright detailed: Nelson several times noted uterus weights when performing autopsies on men, then falsified his notes to correct the errors. The final straw, Wright said, was when Nelson concluded that a woman had died of natural causes, though her husband later confessed to strangling her.
It was Nelson who ruled the death of Pinzon's patient, 70-year-old Rosario Gurrieri, was a homicide. Nelson testified last week he had found lethal levels of morphine in Gurrieri.

Gurrieri was admitted to a Highlands County hospital last October with lung cancer that had spread into his spine and liver as well as other vital organs. His personal physician had given him about two days to live when Pinzon began to treat him.
Gurrieri and his family begged Pinzon for enough drugs to put him in a coma.
It was illness, not the doctor, that killed Gurrieri, Pinzon's lawyers have argued.
Pinzon is charged with first-degree murder. If convicted, he will spend the rest of his life in prison without possibility of parole. The jury is expected to receive the case Thursday.
